screening_decisions.reason: Prospective diagnostic accuracy study evaluating HE4, CA125, ROMA and RMI in 1218 patients with pelvic masses using histopathology as reference standard; directly assesses biomarker and combined test accuracy for ovarian cancer diagnosis.

Prospective cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study of HE4, CA125 and ROMA in 108 women undergoing surgery for pelvic mass with final pathologic results as reference; compares biomarker tests in relevant population.

Single-centre retrospective diagnostic accuracy study based on prospectively collected ultrasound data evaluating the IOTA ADNEX model (with and without CA125) in 278 patients with adnexal masses using histopathology as reference standard.

Retrospective case note audit of general CA125 usage across 799 patients with varied indications; not a diagnostic test accuracy study in women with a pelvic mass suspicious for ovarian cancer and lacks a unified reference standard.

Retrospective diagnostic accuracy study with prospectively collected data externally validating the ADNEX model and comparing it with LR2, simple rules and RMI variants in 326 patients with adnexal masses using pathology as reference.

Systematic review and meta-analysis comparing ROMA and RMI-I; this is a secondary synthesis, not a primary cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study or trial eligible under the selection criteria.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating RMI 1-4 in 408 patients with adnexal masses managed surgically, using histopathology as reference standard and separately analysing premenopausal and postmenopausal women.

Prospective multicentre diagnostic accuracy study comparing HE4, CA125 and ROMA in women including those with benign pelvic masses and epithelial ovarian cancer, reporting accuracy by menopausal status and using pathologic examination as reference.

Study evaluates HE4, CA125 and ROMA in a broad mixed population including healthy women and various benign gynaecological diseases; not specifically focused on women with a pelvic mass suspicious for ovarian cancer.
Systematic review of symptoms associated with ovarian cancer diagnosis; does not evaluate diagnostic test accuracy of ultrasound or biomarker combinations.
Systematic review and meta-analysis comparing ROMA, HE4 and CA125; this is a secondary evidence synthesis, not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study eligible for inclusion.
Global cancer epidemiology report presenting GLOBOCAN incidence and mortality statistics; not a diagnostic test accuracy study.

Prospective multicentre observational diagnostic study developing and validating the ADNEX model (incorporating clinical, CA125 and ultrasound predictors) in 5909 women with ovarian masses using histology as reference standard.
Retrospective diagnostic accuracy study comparing CA-125, HE4, RMI-II and ROMA in 247 women with adnexal neoplasia submitted to surgical treatment using histological diagnosis as reference standard.
Prospective case-control diagnostic accuracy study evaluating HE4 and CA125 individually and in combination using ROMA in 159 women with adnexal masses, with pathology as reference standard.

Study includes healthy controls, benign cysts and endometriosis patients without a defined pelvic mass suspicious for ovarian cancer as the targeted population; also mixes prognostic outcomes, making it less aligned with the diagnostic accuracy focus.

Prospective multicentre diagnostic accuracy study (IOTA3) in 2403 patients with adnexal masses comparing multiple ultrasound strategies, RMI and risk models using histology after surgery as reference standard.

Original development study of the Risk of Malignancy Index combining CA125, ultrasound score and menopausal status in women with benign and malignant pelvic masses; validates a multivariable model for preoperative diagnosis with histology as reference.
Basic science immunohistochemistry and molecular study characterising HE4 tissue expression and secretion; not a clinical diagnostic test accuracy study in women with pelvic masses.

Prospective diagnostic accuracy study comparing CA125, HE4 and ROMA in 373 patients divided into benign, borderline and malignant ovarian tumour groups by pathologic examination, with analysis stratified by menopausal status.

Prospective diagnostic accuracy study evaluating HE4 and CA-125 in 394 women presenting with a suspicious cystic ovarian mass using surgical pathology as reference standard and calculating ROMA sensitivity and specificity.
Study evaluates CA125, HE4 and ROMA in a mixed population including healthy women and general benign gynaecological diseases; not restricted to women with a pelvic mass suspicious for ovarian cancer.

Prospective temporal and external validation diagnostic accuracy study evaluating simple ultrasound rules, subjective assessment, logistic regression models and RMI in 1938 women with adnexal masses using histology as reference standard.

This is an observational diagnostic accuracy study in 260 postmenopausal women with ovarian masses undergoing surgery. It evaluates the Risk of Ovarian Malignancy Algorithm (ROMA), a multivariable model combining HE4 and CA125, against histopathological verification. It reports sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, and accuracy. It meets the selection criteria as a cross-sectional DTA study validating a multivariable model investigating test combinations in women with a pelvic mass suspicious for OC, with histology as the reference standard.

This is an epidemiological modelling study projecting cancer incidence and mortality in the UK to 2035 using age-period-cohort models. It does not evaluate diagnostic test accuracy, compare diagnostic tests, or validate multivariable models for OC diagnosis in women with pelvic masses.

This is a qualitative study exploring women's experiences and perspectives during the peri-diagnostic period of ovarian cancer. It does not assess diagnostic test accuracy or compare tests against a reference standard.

This is a review article discussing the heterogeneity of ovarian carcinomas, histological types, genetic defects, and mouse models. It is not a primary diagnostic accuracy study and does not evaluate tests in women with pelvic masses.

This is a nested case-control study within the Carotene and Retinol Efficacy Trial evaluating prediagnostic serum biomarker concentrations (CA125, HE4, mesothelin) 0-18 years before diagnosis. The population consists of trial participants, not women presenting with a pelvic mass suspicious for OC. The design is nested case-control rather than cross-sectional DTA, and the aim is lead-time assessment rather than diagnostic accuracy in a symptomatic population.

This is a methodological paper describing the development and application of the QUADAS-2 tool for quality assessment of diagnostic accuracy studies in systematic reviews. It is not a primary diagnostic accuracy study evaluating tests for OC.

This study validates cut-points for the Risk of Ovarian Malignancy Algorithm (ROMA) in 207 women presenting with a pelvic mass. It uses the Roche Elecsys CA125 and HE4 assays and compares ROMA scores to definitive histologic diagnosis. This meets the criteria as a study validating a multivariable model investigating test combinations with histological confirmation as the reference standard.

This is a narrative review of the literature on the CA125 tumour-associated antigen. It discusses the nature, distribution, and clinical significance of CA125 but does not present primary diagnostic accuracy data from a cross-sectional study in women with pelvic masses.

This article proposes a model of ovarian tumorigenesis based on morphological and molecular genetic analysis. It is a basic science/pathology review discussing type I and type II tumors and molecular alterations. It does not evaluate diagnostic tests or report diagnostic accuracy.

This is a critical review article discussing proteomic technologies and biomarkers for ovarian cancer. It focuses on experimental technologies and requires further validation, but it is not itself a primary diagnostic accuracy study.

This study investigates the validity of the Risk of Malignancy Index (RMI) — a multivariable score combining ultrasound features, menopausal status, and CA125 — in 540 women with adnexal tumors. It relates RMI scores to histopathological findings and reports sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV separately for premenopausal and postmenopausal women. This meets the criteria as a cross-sectional DTA study evaluating a test combination in women with adnexal masses with histological reference.

This study assesses the diagnostic accuracy of the Risk of Ovarian Malignancy Algorithm (ROMA) in 443 patients with a pelvic mass. ROMA scores (based on HE4 and CA125) were compared against biopsy or clinical follow-up with imaging as the reference standard. It evaluates sensitivity and specificity at different cutoffs and reports accuracy metrics. This meets the criteria as a cross-sectional DTA study evaluating a multivariable model with test combinations.

This study analyzes preoperative multimodal strategies for risk assessment of adnexal masses in 1362 cases. It evaluates expert sonography, CA-125, the Risk of Malignancy Index (RMI), and triage strategies combining these tests. Surgical exploration with histological diagnosis serves as the reference standard. It reports sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV, with analysis stratified by menopausal status. This meets the criteria as a cross-sectional DTA study comparing two or more tests and evaluating test combinations.

This is a prospective multicenter cross-sectional study evaluating the IOTA three-step strategy (simple descriptors, simple rules, and subjective assessment) in 1165 women with adnexal masses, with 301 undergoing surgery. The final outcome was histological diagnosis of surgically removed masses. It compares the IOTA strategy to the Risk of Malignancy Index (RMI) and reports sensitivity and specificity. This meets the criteria as a cross-sectional DTA study comparing tests in women with adnexal masses using histology as the reference standard.

This study assesses the performance of publication bias tests in meta-analyses of diagnostic test accuracy using simulations. It is a methodological/simulation study, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study evaluating tests for ovarian cancer in women with pelvic masses.

This study evaluates the performance of HE4, CA125, and ROMA in 756 patients with pelvic masses (including 275 malignancies and 53 borderline tumors). It assesses areas under the ROC curve for these markers and combinations, and proposes population-specific cut-off values. The classification into benign and malignant diseases implies histological confirmation. This meets the criteria as a cross-sectional DTA study evaluating single tests and a multivariable model algorithm in women with pelvic masses.

This study performs an external validation of the IOTA ADNEX model — a multivariable model for differential diagnosis of adnexal tumors — in two independent gynecologic centers (327 patients total with adnexal masses). It discriminates malignant from benign tumors and attempts to predict specific tumor types, compared against the definitive histological diagnosis. This meets the criteria as a study validating a multivariable model for the diagnosis of OC with histological confirmation in women with adnexal masses.

This is a cohort study evaluating the impact of implementing symptom-triggered diagnostic testing for suspected ovarian cancer in UK hospitals. It assesses referral compliance, stage shift, and workload outcomes, but does not evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of test combinations, compare diagnostic tests, or validate multivariable models against a reference standard of histology or clinical follow-up in a defined pelvic mass population.

This multicenter prospective study enrolls women with a pelvic mass scheduled for surgery. Preoperative HE4 and CA125 were measured, and separate logistic regression algorithms for premenopausal and postmenopausal women categorized patients into low and high risk groups for epithelial ovarian cancer. The reference standard was surgical histopathology (benign, EOC, LMP). It reports sensitivity and specificity for the algorithm. This meets the criteria as a study validating a multivariable model investigating test combinations with histological confirmation.

This is a clinical guidelines document providing recommendations for the evaluation and management of adnexal masses in adolescents, pregnant women, and nonpregnant women. It is not a primary research study reporting diagnostic accuracy data from a cross-sectional or randomized design.

This is a molecular genetics study investigating ARID1A mutations and BAF250a protein loss in ovarian clear-cell and endometrioid carcinomas. It involves sequencing and immunohistochemical analysis but does not evaluate diagnostic test accuracy or validate multivariable diagnostic models in women with pelvic masses.

The available abstract indicates this is a narrative overview discussing the benefits of HE4 compared to traditional tumor markers in gynecological oncology. It does not describe a primary study design, a defined population with pelvic masses, a reference standard, or diagnostic accuracy metrics. It appears to be a review or commentary rather than a cross-sectional DTA study.

This prospective multicenter study includes 414 women with an adnexal mass scheduled for surgery from six Asian countries. Preoperative CA125 and HE4 were measured, and ROMA scores were calculated. The study evaluates sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV of HE4, CA125, and ROMA for distinguishing benign from malignant pelvic masses, using histological diagnosis as the reference standard. This meets the criteria as a cross-sectional DTA study evaluating single tests and a multivariable model combination in women with pelvic masses.

Epidemiological incidence-trends study using cancer registry data. It does not evaluate diagnostic tests, compare tests, or validate multivariable models against a reference standard in women with pelvic masses suspicious for ovarian cancer.
Systematic review and meta-analysis of primary studies, not a primary cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study, RCT, or multivariable model validation.

Prospective trial evaluating the ROMA index (combination of CA125, HE4, and menopausal status) for prediction of malignancy in women with adnexal masses scheduled for operation, using pathological results as the reference standard. Meets cross-sectional DTA criteria.

Prospective multicentre cross-sectional study validating IOTA prediction models (LR2, Simple Rules) and RMI against histological diagnosis in women with adnexal masses. Evaluates test combinations with appropriate reference standard.
Meta-analysis pooling studies of CA125, HE4, and ROMA. Not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study.

Prospective cross-sectional study comparing CA-125, HE4, RMI, and ROMA in women with ovarian lesions who underwent surgical intervention, using histopathological diagnosis as the gold standard. Evaluates single and combined tests.

Multicenter study evaluating HE4, CA125, and ROMA in women with suspicious pelvic masses requiring surgery, with final diagnoses including benign disease, borderline neoplasia, and tumors. Uses surgical identification as the reference standard and includes pre- and postmenopausal women.
Methodological paper describing hierarchical regression models for meta-analysis of diagnostic test accuracy. Not a primary DTA study in women with pelvic masses.
Simulation study assessing the performance of meta-analytic methods. Not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study.
Study examining inherited germline mutations for cancer predisposition using genetic sequencing. Not a diagnostic test accuracy study for ovarian cancer in women with pelvic masses.
Narrative review covering prevention, detection, and treatment strategies. Not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study, RCT, or multivariable model validation.

Prospective multicenter blinded clinical trial validating ROMA (using HE4 and CA125) in women presenting with an adnexal/pelvic mass. Reports sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV against malignancy outcomes.
Prospective study evaluating four malignancy risk indices (RMI 1-4) in women admitted for surgical exploration of pelvic masses. Assesses diagnostic performance for malignant ovarian tumors.

Study investigating RMI variants, CA-125, and inflammatory markers for discriminating ovarian cancers in postmenopausal women with adnexal masses who underwent surgery. Uses surgical outcomes as the reference standard.

Study evaluating HE4, CA125, and ROMA for preoperative differentiation of benign and malignant adnexal masses, stratified by menopausal status, using histologically verified diagnoses. Evaluates biomarker combinations relevant to the review.

Population-based case-control study examining symptoms of ovarian cancer in primary care. Does not evaluate ultrasound or biomarker tests for diagnosis in women with pelvic masses suspicious for ovarian cancer.

Prospective validation study of ROMA in women with a pelvic mass scheduled for surgery. Measures preoperative HE4 and CA125 and evaluates diagnostic performance including in pre- and postmenopausal subgroups.
Systematic review and meta-analysis of prediction models for presurgical diagnosis. Not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study.

Study comparing CA125, HE4, ROMA, and RMI for classification of ovarian masses. Evaluates sensitivity and specificity for distinguishing malignant versus benign masses, consistent with a diagnostic test accuracy design.
Statement/guideline on inherited cancer predisposition risk assessment (e.g., BRCA, Lynch syndrome). Not a diagnostic test accuracy study for ovarian cancer in women with pelvic masses.

Cross-sectional study evaluating standard and optimal cut-offs of CA-125, HE4, and ROMA in women with ovarian masses, matched to postoperative histopathology. Reports diagnostic accuracy measures by menopausal status.
Study evaluating HE4, CA125, and ROMA2 index in postmenopausal women with histologically verified benign or malignant ovarian tumors, with serum collected prior to surgery or treatment.

Study evaluating preoperative 2D ultrasound, CA125, 3DPD, RMI, IOTA simple rules, and LR2 in postmenopausal women with ovarian tumors, with results compared postoperatively to histopathological results. Evaluates multiple test combinations.

This is a systematic review and meta-analysis comparing HE4 versus CA125, not a primary cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study, randomized trial, or multivariable model validation study in women with pelvic masses.

Diagnostic accuracy study enrolling 129 patients with pelvic mass(es) suspected of ovarian origin undergoing surgery or biopsy. Evaluates HE4, CA125, and the ROMA combination against a surgical/histological reference standard. Meets all selection criteria for population, intervention, and design.

Prospective study of women presenting with complex pelvic masses evaluating HE4, CA125, ROMA, and RMI against histological reference standard. Fits the review's scope of test combinations for ovarian cancer diagnosis in women with pelvic masses.

Methodological paper describing the PROBAST tool for assessing risk of bias in prediction model studies. Not a diagnostic accuracy study evaluating tests for ovarian cancer in women with pelvic masses.

Study of women with pelvic masses evaluating the ROMA algorithm (HE4 + CA125 combination) for epithelial ovarian cancer diagnosis, with separate algorithms for pre- and postmenopausal women, using surgery as the reference standard. Meets all selection criteria.

Study categorizing routes to cancer diagnosis using linked administrative data. Not a diagnostic test accuracy study evaluating biomarkers, ultrasound, or multivariable models in women with pelvic masses suspicious for ovarian cancer.
Methodological paper comparing bivariate meta-analysis versus summary ROC approaches for diagnostic reviews. Not a primary diagnostic accuracy study for ovarian cancer.

Prospective population-based study of women with pelvic masses scheduled for surgery. Evaluates RMI versus ROMA and CA125 versus HE4 with pathology as the reference standard. Meets population, intervention, design, and reference standard criteria.
User guide for a SAS macro (MetaDAS) for meta-analysis of diagnostic accuracy studies. Not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study.

Meta-analysis comparing ROMA, HE4, and CA125 for epithelial ovarian cancer prediction. Not a primary cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study, randomized trial, or multivariable model validation study.

Study using a multicenter IOTA database of patients with adnexal masses evaluating IOTA logistic regression models (multivariable models), IOTA simple rules, and RMI against histological diagnosis. Evaluates test combinations and multivariable models in women with pelvic masses.

Subset analysis of a prospective clinical trial enrolling women undergoing surgery for an adnexal mass. Evaluates HE4 and CA125 for epithelial ovarian cancer detection against pathology in premenopausal women with pelvic masses.

Case-control study (123 ovarian cancer patients and 174 controls) evaluating HE4 for ROMA prediction and prognosis/therapy monitoring. Population does not consist of women with pelvic masses suspicious for ovarian cancer, and the study includes prognostic outcomes beyond the review's diagnostic scope.

Study of 1,042 women with benign disease only (no malignant cases) prior to surgery for pelvic mass. Without malignant cases, diagnostic accuracy for ovarian cancer cannot be assessed. Not a diagnostic test accuracy study for ovarian cancer.
Review article discussing biomarkers for screening, diagnosis, and monitoring of ovarian cancer. Not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study.

Biomarker development study describing HE4 ELISA and testing on postmenopausal ovarian carcinoma patients and controls. Case-control design with healthy controls rather than women with pelvic masses suspicious for ovarian cancer.
Systematic review of risk scores for predicting ovarian malignancy. Not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study, randomized trial, or multivariable model validation study.
Diagnostic accuracy study of sentinel lymph node biopsy for lymph node involvement in endometrial cancer. Wrong condition (endometrial cancer, not ovarian cancer).
Meta-analysis of IOTA simple rules for ovarian cancer diagnosis. Not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study.

Study evaluating CA125, HE4, and ROMA in 762 patients with benign gynecological disease and 70 with ovarian cancer. Population includes mixed benign gynecological conditions (uterine myoma, adenomyosis, endometrial pathology, endometriosis) rather than women with pelvic masses suspicious for ovarian cancer. Design is case-control rather than cross-sectional in the target population.
Review article assessing the usefulness of diagnostic indices combining clinical, sonographic, and biomarker data for ovarian masses. Not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study.

Multicenter clinical trial validating HE4, CA125, ROMA, and RMI in 638 women diagnosed with an unknown ovarian cyst or pelvic tumor, with final pathology as the reference standard. Diagnostic accuracy study of test combinations in the target population.

Study comparing the ADNEX multivariable model with subjective assessment in women who underwent adnexal surgery with abnormal pelvic ultrasound findings. Evaluates a multivariable model for differentiating benign and malignant adnexal masses with pathology reference standard.
